# Is there room for a third chair between the pallet stack and the two metal chairs?

## Short answer

**Yes.** There is enough space between the right-hand side of the wooden pallet stack and the left-hand metal chair to fit one more chair of the same size. It would be a fairly snug fit — roughly one and a quarter chair widths of gap — but a third chair would go in, and it would only be room for one more, not two.

## What is in the scene

The two grey metal folding chairs stand in the foreground of a stack of brown cardboard watermelon cartons (printed 花蓮新蘭 西瓜), which themselves rest on a blue plastic pallet. To the left of the chairs, in the same row and at essentially the same distance from the camera, is a stack of wooden pallets with white and blue cartons piled on top of it. In front of all of this, closer to the camera, is the display of open cardboard trays of apples, mangoes, kiwifruit and oranges. The chairs occupy a narrow open strip of floor between the fruit-tray display in front of them and the brown cartons behind them, and the question is whether that strip continues far enough to the left, clear of obstruction, to take a third chair.

## Measurements

Working in the coordinates of the original 4032 × 3024 image:

- The right-hand edge of the wooden pallet stack sits at about x = 835.
- The left chair spans about x = 1120 to x = 1355 at its widest (its splayed legs), and about x = 1131 to x = 1333 across its seat and backrest. Its projected width is therefore roughly 200–240 pixels.
- The right chair spans about x = 1409 to x = 1599, so the two chairs are separated from each other by only about 75 pixels — they sit almost shoulder to shoulder.
- The clear horizontal gap between the pallet stack and the left chair is therefore about 285 pixels.

That gap of roughly 285 pixels is about 1.2 to 1.4 times the projected width of a single chair. In real terms the gap is on the order of 90 cm to 1 m, while a folding chair of this kind needs about 45–50 cm of width (its projected footprint here, seen at a slight angle, reads as around 60 cm).

The comparison is fair because the pallet stack and the chairs are at practically the same depth: the bottom front edge of the lowest wooden pallet is at about y = 2045, and the chair legs are still descending past y = 2040 where the fruit trays cut them off. Since the two are in the same depth band, comparing their horizontal pixel extents directly is valid rather than misleading.

## Visual check

I tested this by copying the left chair out of the image and pasting it into the gap with its left side flush against the pallet stack. The pasted chair sits in the space naturally and still leaves a visible gap of about 40–50 pixels between it and the original left chair — comparable to the 75-pixel gap that already separates the two real chairs. This confirms the arithmetic: one extra chair fits, with a small margin, and a fourth would not.

## Caveats

Two things I could not verify directly, and which slightly qualify the answer:

- The floor itself in that gap is not visible in the photograph. It is hidden behind the foreground fruit trays, so I am inferring that the strip of floor is clear from the fact that the same strip, immediately to the right, is clear enough to hold the two existing chairs.
- At the base of the gap there is a blue plastic pallet or crate under the brown cartons, occupying roughly x = 840 to x = 970 at floor level. This sits behind the line the chairs stand on, but it could stop a third chair from being pushed as far back against the cartons as the existing two are.

Neither of these changes the width conclusion. The lateral space between the pallet stack and the two chairs is wider than a chair, so a third chair would fit there.

The two metal chairs referred to are the two light-grey folding chairs standing side-by-side in the mid-ground, facing forward, directly in front of the two-high stack of brown boxes printed with a watermelon logo, red Chinese text and a red circular stamp.

The stack of wooden pallets referred to is the tall stack of light-colored wooden pallets on the left side of the image, with boxes including a blue and white CHELAN box sitting on top of it.

The pallet stack is to the left of the chairs. The lateral interval at the depth of the chairs, from the right face of the pallet stack to the left side of the left-hand metal chair, is wider than one metal chair.

This can be seen by using the brown boxes behind as a ruler. Each metal chair is about one brown-box wide in the image. Between the right edge of the pallet stack and the left leg and left side of the left chair there are about one-and-a-half to two brown-box widths of frontage. In the enlarged view the left chair back spans roughly the width of one box, while the empty frontage to its left spans almost two boxes before the pallet wood begins.

The floor on that interval is the same concrete floor strip on which the two existing chairs stand, immediately in front of the brown boxes and their blue base pallet. It is not occupied by any fixed structure. The low open fruit boxes in the nearer foreground sit forward of the chair line and do not block that strip, just as they do not block the two existing chairs.

A third folding chair placed upright in line with the existing two, facing the same direction, would therefore fit between the pallet stack and the leftmost chair without overlapping either.
